personas.subtitle: Management accountant, public-sector adviser and former Olympic skier
personas.summary: Peter is a senior management accountant and a regular consultant to political leadership in Ottawa. He has advised most federal departments, serves on the Canada Revenue Agency departmental audit committee, participates in financial-standard and anti-money-laundering working groups, and has held security clearances including an above-top-secret clearance for work involving FINTRAC. Earlier, he was a grant-funded academic and competed in alpine skiing at the 1998 Nagano Olympics with support from Sport Canada and other federal bodies. He immigrated from Lebanon at age four or five and became a Canadian citizen in early high school. He is divorced, owns one shotgun, has a boating licence, holds a passport, travels frequently to the United States, and uses NEXUS. Transport Canada investigated a boating accident involving him in 1997. He has directed corporations and has owned a sole proprietorship and a trust.

expected_ambiguities: Consulting inside departments can sound like federal employment, but a contractor should normally route through federal contracting, not employee PIBs.
A departmental audit committee appointment may have its own institution-specific records that the federal-contract selector does not isolate.
Tri-council grants and Sport Canada athlete support both fall into a broad payment fallback and should be separate named routes.
Transport Canada's 1997 safety investigation is not clearly represented by the generic justice fallback.
A divorce by itself does not establish that a federal institution holds a record; the family-life-event wording may overmatch.
A boating licence may mean a Pleasure Craft Operator Card, a pleasure craft licence, or vessel registration; this fixture assumes the operator card only.
Above-top-secret is retained as user-provided biographical wording, but the survey only sends the controlled security-screening route.
known_false_positive_risks: government employee records from consultant work
unrelated grant and benefit programs from fallback routing

personas.subtitle: Former contractor with a long history of federal investigations and corrections
personas.summary: Dominic is a fictional Canadian-born former construction subcontractor and courier. Over three decades he accumulated convictions for fraud, trafficking and weapons offences, served more than one federal sentence, and was repeatedly investigated by the RCMP, Canada Border Services Agency, Canada Revenue Agency and integrated proceeds-of-crime teams. A cross-border smuggling investigation involved a small vessel and customs seizure. His firearms licence was revoked, his parole has been suspended and restored more than once, and he has appealed correctional and parole decisions. He later sought his own records through access-to-information and personal-information requests. He has also received Employment Insurance, held a CMHC-insured mortgage, owned a sole proprietorship, registered a vessel, filed federal taxes inconsistently, voted, held a passport and crossed the border. No ethnic, religious or racial identity is assigned to this criminal-history test persona.

experience.details: Operated vehicles and a small registered vessel; business ended after a border investigation.

education: High-school equivalency completed while in custody

Former owner of a federally registered small vessel
Received Employment Insurance during periods outside custody

episodes.details: A small vessel was stopped during a customs and smuggling investigation; Dominic challenged the seizure decision.

expected_ambiguities: Being investigated does not mean every RCMP investigative PIB applies; the police route intentionally has partial coverage and can overmatch.
The engine does not distinguish investigation, charge, conviction, victim, witness or collateral contact roles.
Correctional health care is a federal health interaction, but the current health fallback does not isolate Correctional Service Canada health records.
Tax-compliance and criminal-investigation records are not represented by the tax-return inventory-gap route.
A CMHC-insured mortgage is hidden behind a generic housing fallback.
Old revoked licences and vessel records are useful retention stress tests, but disposition depends on trigger events not captured by the survey.
known_false_positive_risks: all Correctional Service Canada offender banks
unrelated health and housing programs from fallback routing

personas.subtitle: Community nonprofit coordinator and federal funding partner
personas.summary: Aisha coordinates a small fictional nonprofit community hub in Nova Scotia. She has never worked for government and has no criminal, military or regulatory history. Her federal interactions mainly arise from contribution agreements and community participation: the organization receives grants from Employment and Social Development Canada, Women and Gender Equality Canada and Canadian Heritage; she joins consultations, submits program reports, volunteers in a federally supported newcomer program and answers evaluation surveys. During 2023 wildfires she requested federal logistics support for the hub. Earlier she used Canada Student Loans. She files taxes annually, votes, holds a passport and made one recent trip abroad. She does not own a firearm or boat and has not used a federal health or housing program.

expected_ambiguities: A nonprofit employee administering contribution agreements may not consider herself the recipient of a benefit, grant or payment.
Operating a nonprofit is not the same as owning a business or being a federal supplier, making the business question legitimately uncertain.
Current broad grant fallback cannot distinguish the funding departments or contribution-agreement program records.
A federally funded volunteer activity is not necessarily federally run; the current wording can create a false positive.
Program evaluation surveys should route to the funding institution, not only generic Health Canada research PIBs.
Emergency assistance requested on behalf of an organization may create organizational rather than personal records.

federal volunteer records where the program is only federally funded
personal emergency-service records for an organizational request

personas.subtitle: Former federal employee dismissed, reinstated after grievance, then departed
personas.summary: Sophie worked in federal program administration from 2008 to 2024. After several poor-performance assessments and an internal administrative investigation, Employment and Social Development Canada dismissed her in 2022. Her union grievance alleged failures in accommodation and procedural fairness; adjudication led to reinstatement in 2023 with back pay and corrected leave records. A renewed reliability screening followed. She requested her personnel and investigation files, sought corrections to personal information, and later left government in 2024 after another performance dispute. She received Employment Insurance, had federal pay and pension adjustments, and participated in employee surveys. Earlier she used Canada Student Loans and later used a federally supported home-buying program. She is divorced and had a child-support reassessment. She files taxes, votes, has a passport and travelled internationally, but has no military, criminal, firearms or boating history.

expected_ambiguities: A dismissal, grievance, reinstatement and final departure need separate event dates; one timing for federal employment cannot express that sequence.
The generic complaint fallback cannot distinguish a labour grievance, adjudication, staffing complaint or human-rights complaint.
Workplace accommodation and disability records may live in employee, benefits and institution-specific systems rather than a generic federal-health program.
An internal administrative investigation is not necessarily federal law enforcement and should not be inferred from the security-screening answer.
Back pay, regular pay, pension adjustment and Employment Insurance have different institutions and retention triggers.
Divorce and child-support administration can be provincial, federal tax-related or interjurisdictional; a generic life-event fallback overmatches.
